questions.scenario: Two massive, rival groups in your coaching institute are about to break into a big fight over bench rows. What do you do?

options.text: Blend into the crowd quietly, listen to what both sides are secretly plotting, and keep a close eye on their leaders.
Sit back and analyze the past history of why these two groups hate each other and how it impacts the whole batch's discipline.
Take out your phone to record the drama, interview bystanders, and write a super juicy summary for the batch's backbenchers group chat.
Step in as a mediator, negotiate a compromise where they split the middle benches, and establish strict rules for tomorrow.

questions.scenario: Your grandfather or Uncle starts a heated discussion at the dinner table about a major global news event involving India. What is your input?

options.text: Ask about how our border forces or secret agents handle such high-alert situations on the ground.
Explain the background history, comparing how global economic trade routes and historic treaties are forcing this situation.
Rant about how television news anchors are hyping it up completely wrong and explain how you would explain it to the public clearly.
Argue about what the Indian Ministry of External Affairs or National Security Advisor should do next to protect our country's safety.

questions.scenario: You are playing a hardcore strategy board game like Risk, Catan, or Monopoly with your cousins. What is your winning style?

options.text: Forming secret, unwritten pacts with one cousin while keeping tabs on another's resources to strike at the perfect moment.
Studying the game map deeply, calculating resource distributions, and predicting every player's moves based on their patterns.
Creating a highly entertaining running commentary of the match, calling out everyone's betrayals dramatically to the audience.
Acting as the dominant banker/leader, allocating territory fairly to prevent any one cousin from becoming too powerful.

questions.scenario: You are chosen to participate in your school's annual Model United Nations (MUN). What is your ideal strategy?

options.text: Slipping handwritten chits across the committee room to secretly gather support and block a rival country's resolution.
Spending nights reading thick research dossiers to find factual loopholes in the opposing delegate's foreign policy speech.
Drafting an incredibly powerful, emotional, and catchy opening speech that gets the entire committee hall staring at you.
Forming a powerful multi-nation alliance in the lobby and drafting the final resolution paper that solves the global crisis.

questions.scenario: An intense India vs Pakistan cricket match is happening. What keeps you hooked besides the actual runs scored?

options.text: Watching the players' subtle body language on screen to figure out what their hidden team game-plan or frustration points are.
Analyzing the tournament statistics, head-to-head history, and pitch data to see if the odds favor our team.
Following the crazy social media banter, memes, and fan stories coming from both sides of the border.
Thinking about how the team management should line up the bowling order or adapt their strategy if a sudden wicket falls.

questions.scenario: You are browsing through YouTube or Instagram. Which type of video stops you in your tracks instantly?

options.text: A thrilling documentary detailing how real-life operations or cross-border tracking missions are successfully planned.
A breakdown channel (like Johnny Harris or Think School) explaining the maps, oil economics, and history of current world conflicts.
A ground-level video report showing the actual day-to-day lives of people living in far-off, high-tension global zones.
An interview with a retired diplomat or minister breaking down how India negotiates massive global trade deals.

questions.scenario: Your school group needs to borrow a high-end DSLR camera from a notoriously strict senior for a fest project. How do you help?

options.text: Find out what that senior likes or who their best friend is, using that inner loop info to approach them easily.
Look back at who borrowed it in the past and research the exact guidelines the senior sets to make sure you fulfill them.
Pitch an amazing, creative vision of the final video project to the senior so they get excited to lend you the gear.
Offer a formal deal where your team handles the camera safely and gives the senior a prime credit slot in the school fest pamphlet.

questions.scenario: You have to choose a topic for a 10th standard social science presentation. Which of these appeals to you the most?

options.text: How border security technology and surveillance radars are deployed to stop illegal smuggling on Indian borders.
How the cold war era shaped modern alliances and changed the economy of Asian countries.
A compilation of real letters, pictures, and emotional diaries of civilians caught during historic global evacuations.
A case study on how India's 'Non-Aligned Movement' or 'Panchsheel' policies protected our interests for decades.

questions.scenario: Imagine there is a massive cybersecurity rumor floating around that a foreign app is stealing student chat data. What is your stance?

options.text: Immediately check your phone's background data logs and app permissions to see what info is actually being tracked on the ground.
Read up on where the app's servers are located and analyze why this specific country is trying to gain data access right now.
Write a warnings post or script a quick informative video explaining the whole situation simply to save your classmates from panic.
Draft a formal application to the school principal suggesting a safe, alternate Indian app for school projects.

questions.scenario: Your family is planning a long vacation across different states in India. What part of planning do you jump into?

options.text: Mapping out the specific remote pit-stops, safe overnight spots, and tracking emergency contact centers along the highways.
Reading about the rich culture, historic monuments, and economic shifts of that region to understand it deeply before visiting.
Shortlisting the most photogenic cultural lanes, local markets, and traditional food stalls to create a travel vlog.
Managing the total travel budget, booking flights/trains, and coordinating the schedule to maximize time without burnout.

Intelligence_Officer.title: The Silent Shield (Field Intelligence Officer / Agent)
Intelligence_Officer.primary_match_text: You are a master of observation and ground-level action! You thrive on gathering raw information, keeping secrets, reading human behavior, and protecting security silently behind the scenes.
Intelligence_Officer.day_in_the_life: Monitoring borders, coordinating covert operations, analyzing live field data from ground networks, and tracking security vulnerabilities to keep the nation safe.
Intelligence_Officer.alternative_match_text: Your sharp instincts and tactical mindset would also make you a brilliant Defense Officer in the Armed Forces, Cyber-Security Investigator, or Operations Lead.
Intelligence_Officer.educational_roadmap: 11th/12th Arts/Humanities or Any Stream -> BA in Political Science, History, or Cyber Security -> Appear for UPSC Civil Services Exam (for IPS/IFS) or clear direct exams like SSC CGL or Assistant Central Intelligence Officer (ACIO) tests for central security bureaus.

Geopolitical_Analyst.title: The Global Chessmaster (Geopolitical Think-Tank Researcher)
Geopolitical_Analyst.primary_match_text: You have a stellar analytical mind! You love reading between the lines, connecting the dots between world history, international trade, economics, and warfare to predict the next global event.
Geopolitical_Analyst.day_in_the_life: Reading thick foreign policy drafts, writing research reports for global think tanks, analyzing satellite map data, and analyzing how oil or chip supply chains affect India's market.
Geopolitical_Analyst.alternative_match_text: Your incredible research skills and love for patterns would also make you a top-notch Risk Consultant, Market Research Director, or Economic Historian.
Geopolitical_Analyst.educational_roadmap: 11th/12th Arts/Humanities (History, Economics, Pol Sci preferred) -> BA in International Relations or Political Science -> MA/Ph.D. in Global Studies or Strategic Affairs -> Join prestigious Indian think tanks like IDSA or ORF.

International_Journalist.title: The Global Storyteller (International Journalist / Documentarian)
International_Journalist.primary_match_text: You are a creative communicator with unmatched courage! You believe complex international conflicts or treaties shouldn't just stay in files; they need to be explained vividly to ordinary citizens through storytelling.
International_Journalist.day_in_the_life: Traveling to foreign capitals, interviewing global leaders and local citizens, scripting hard-hitting video essays, and broadcasting breaking global stories from high-tension locations.
International_Journalist.alternative_match_text: Your knack for communication and visual storytelling would make you an outstanding Documentary Filmmaker, Foreign Correspondent, or Public Relations specialist.
International_Journalist.educational_roadmap: 11th/12th Humanities/Arts or Any Stream -> BJMC (Bachelor of Journalism and Mass Communication) or BA in English Literature/Political Science -> PG Diploma in Journalism from institutes like IIMC or ACJ.

Strategic_Advisor.title: The Diplomatic Commander (Strategic Policy Advisor / Diplomat)
Strategic_Advisor.primary_match_text: You are a natural, visionary leader! You excel at high-stakes negotiations, managing major crises, and advising senior leaders on how to steer national policy and global defense strategies.
Strategic_Advisor.day_in_the_life: Drafting briefing notes for cabinet ministers, attending high-profile global summits, negotiating bilateral trade treaties, and managing foreign relations during unexpected diplomatic crises.
Strategic_Advisor.alternative_match_text: Your strategic leadership and negotiation skills make you ideal for roles like Corporate Strategy Head, International Lawyer, or Management Consultant.
Strategic_Advisor.educational_roadmap: 11th/12th Arts/Humanities or Commerce -> BA/B.Sc in Economics, Law, or Political Science -> Clear the prestigious UPSC Civil Services Examination to enter the Indian Foreign Service (IFS) or pursue a Master's in Public Policy.
